task_1.title: Fix nested macro caller block scoping
task_1.description: Upgrading to 2.9.1 fixes a rendering regression in macro call block scoping. Nested caller blocks now resolve reused identifiers against the correct surrounding scope, preventing templates from rendering with values taken from the wrong variable when macros forward caller content.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that nested macro caller blocks resolve variables using the correct scope so that reusing the same identifiers across outer macros and inner caller blocks does not render the wrong value.

expectation.grounded: When templates use macros, `call` blocks, and forwarded `caller` callbacks together, identifier lookup for the nested macro call must follow the surrounding render frame at the call site. If an inner caller block reuses an identifier name that also exists in an outer macro scope, rendering should bind that name to the correct visible value instead of the wrong variable from another macro scope.
expectation.conceptual: Nested macro callbacks should behave with consistent lexical scoping. Reusing variable names in inner and outer macro contexts must not cause rendered output to pull data from the wrong scope.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing public macro, `call`, and `caller` behavior apart from the scoping regression. Templates that do not rely on conflicting identifier names in nested caller scenarios should continue to render the same, and the fix must not change the normal ability to pass values through nested caller invocations.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to correcting incorrect scope resolution. Existing macro rendering patterns should continue to work unless they were previously affected by this bug.

behavior: Nested macro calls that forward `caller` should resolve names using the scope visible where the call is written, not an incorrect inner caller scope.

If a nested caller block and an enclosing macro reuse the same identifier name, rendering should use the intended value for that nested caller invocation rather than a shadowed value from the wrong scope.
Templates that chain macros through `call` and `caller(...)` should produce stable output even when outer and inner scopes use overlapping parameter names.
acceptance_criteria: When a template nests macros and `call` blocks and both inner and outer scopes define the same identifier, rendering should use the value that is in scope at the nested call site.

When a macro forwards a `caller` callback into another macro, invoking that nested caller should render content with the correct arguments and scope bindings, without accidentally reading a same-named variable from an outer macro.
When macros and `call` blocks do not involve conflicting names, rendering behavior should remain unchanged by the upgrade.
